title: A to-do list in four steps
note: Written by hand as a sample of the format. Each check is Tcl that the player runs in the live window, and tests/replay.sh runs in ztk --headless.

steps.say: Make a to-do list: a field for a new item, an Add button, and the list.
The window has an entry and a button in a row, and a listbox under them. The first column of the grid grows with the window.
steps.script:
ttk::entry .new -width 28
ttk::button .add -text Add
listbox .items -height 6
grid .new .add -sticky ew -padx 8 -pady 8
grid .items - -sticky nsew -padx 8
grid columnconfigure . 0 -weight 1
steps.check:
update
expr {[winfo class .items] eq "Listbox" && [winfo ismapped .new] && [winfo ismapped .add]}

steps.say: Add works now? Return in the field should add too.
Add and Return call the proc add. It trims the text, skips an empty item, and clears the field. The list has two items to try.
steps.script:
proc add {} {
    set text [string trim [.new get]]
    if {$text eq ""} return
    .items insert end $text
    .new delete 0 end
}
ttk::entry .new -width 28 -placeholder "What needs doing?"
ttk::button .add -text Add -command add
listbox .items -height 6
bind .new <Return> add
grid .new .add -sticky ew -padx 8 -pady 8
grid .items - -sticky nsew -padx 8
grid columnconfigure . 0 -weight 1
.items insert end "Buy milk" "Write the docs"
steps.check:
focus .new
update
ztk::inject . text "Call Ada"
ztk::inject . key Return
update
expr {[.items size] == 3}

steps.say: I need to mark items done, and see how many are left.
Mark done removes the selected items. A label under the list shows the count after each change.
steps.script:
proc add {} {
    set text [string trim [.new get]]
    if {$text eq ""} return
    .items insert end $text
    .new delete 0 end
    count
}
proc done {} {
    foreach i [lsort -integer -decreasing [.items curselection]] { .items delete $i }
    count
}
proc count {} { set ::status "[.items size] to do" }
ttk::entry .new -width 28 -placeholder "What needs doing?"
ttk::button .add -text Add -command add
listbox .items -height 6 -selectmode extended
ttk::button .done -text "Mark done" -command done
ttk::label .status -textvariable status
bind .new <Return> add
grid .new .add -sticky ew -padx 8 -pady 8
grid .items - -sticky nsew -padx 8
grid .status .done -sticky ew -padx 8 -pady 8
grid columnconfigure . 0 -weight 1
.items insert end "Buy milk" "Write the docs"
count
steps.check:
focus .new
update
ztk::inject . text "Call Ada"
ztk::inject . key Return
.items selection set 0
done
expr {$::status eq "2 to do"}

steps.say: Make the Add button stand out.
The Add button uses the style Accent.TButton: white text on blue, and a darker blue when the pointer is over it.
steps.script:
proc add {} {
    set text [string trim [.new get]]
    if {$text eq ""} return
    .items insert end $text
    .new delete 0 end
    count
}
proc done {} {
    foreach i [lsort -integer -decreasing [.items curselection]] { .items delete $i }
    count
}
proc count {} { set ::status "[.items size] to do" }
ttk::entry .new -width 28 -placeholder "What needs doing?"
ttk::style configure Accent.TButton -foreground white -background #2563eb
ttk::style map Accent.TButton -background {active #1d4ed8}
ttk::button .add -text Add -command add -style Accent.TButton
listbox .items -height 6 -selectmode extended
ttk::button .done -text "Mark done" -command done
ttk::label .status -textvariable status
bind .new <Return> add
grid .new .add -sticky ew -padx 8 -pady 8
grid .items - -sticky nsew -padx 8
grid .status .done -sticky ew -padx 8 -pady 8
grid columnconfigure . 0 -weight 1
.items insert end "Buy milk" "Write the docs"
count
